title: The Telescope Lab
summary: Fill a scope’s ring, fit the Moon on a photo plate and set a telescope for a relaxed or a near-point view.
subject: physics
concepts: Image size from the focal length
Final image at the near point
learningOutcome: The student can use M = f_o/f_e and L = f_o + f_e in normal adjustment, find the size of the real image from f_o × θ, and set a telescope for a final image at the near point.

levels.title: The scout’s scope
levels.adds: Baseline: in normal adjustment M = f_o/f_e and the tube is f_o + f_e long, with the final image at infinity (Ex 9.13, 9.14a, 9.27a).
hints: Angular magnification in normal adjustment is M = f_o/f_e, so f_e = f_o/M.
The objective’s image of a far object is at its focus, so the eyepiece sits f_e beyond that point: L = f_o + f_e.
Set the eyepiece focal length first, then the tube length.

levels.title: The photo plate
levels.adds: New idea: the objective alone forms a real image of size f_o × θ, so the focal length decides how much of the plate the target fills (Ex 9.14b, 9.28b).
hints: The real image of a far object has size f_o × θ, where θ is the angle it covers in radians.
For the Moon θ = 3.48 × 10⁶ / 3.8 × 10⁸ ≈ 0.0092 rad. For the tower, θ = 100/3000 = 1/30 rad.
So f_o = plate size ÷ θ. Round to the nearest 10 cm.

levels.title: Orion’s near-point view
levels.adds: New idea: with the final image at the near point, M = (f_o/f_e)(1 + f_e/D) and the tube is f_o + f_eD/(f_e + D) long (Ex 9.27b).
hints: The eyepiece’s object must be at u_e = f_eD/(f_e + D) from it so its image falls at D = 25 cm.
Then L = f_o + u_e, and M = f_o/u_e.
Solve M = f_o/f_e + f_o/D for f_e, then find L.

misconceptions: A telescope magnifies by making a bigger real image on the retina side of the eyepiece
The tube length of a telescope is always f_o + f_e, whatever the final image distance
A longer objective focal length makes the image of a far object smaller
